description: A list of Free Software network services and web applications which can be hosted on your own servers

summary.one_liner: A curated, categorized list of Free Software network services and web applications that can be self-hosted on your own servers.
summary.what_it_does: This is a link list rather than software. It catalogs Free Software network services and web applications that people can run on their own server(s), as an alternative to SaaS providers. Non-free software is said to be on a separate Non-Free page. Entries are grouped into many categories such as Analytics, Media Streaming, Password Managers, Wikis, Network Utilities, Money/Budgeting, and Software Development. Each entry gives a one-line description, a license code, and the implementation language or deployment method (for example Docker, deb, or Nodejs), with optional links to demos, source code, and clients. The README includes a table of contents, back-to-top links, and cross-references between related categories.
use_cases: find a self-hosted alternative to a SaaS product
browse open source apps by category
pick a media server or music streamer to run at home
find a self-hosted analytics or budgeting tool
compare license and deployment options for self-hosted apps
discover privacy-focused web applications to host
notable: Organized into dozens of categories with a table of contents and cross-links between related sections
Each entry tags license (e.g. AGPL-3.0, MIT) and deployment method (Docker, deb, K8S, language)
Marks entries with a warning symbol (⚠) in the list, and separates Free Software from Non-Free software on a different page
Entries often link to live demos and source code
caveats: The list is not software; it only points to other projects, which may be unmaintained or change license
Some entries are marked with a warning symbol, and the README does not define what the symbol means in the visible portion
The README was truncated in the provided text, so later categories were not visible
